label: D2 arrival at S1 after a rewarded trial (first half of episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 when the reached state shown is S1 (never at D1/GO, never on S2): (phase==D2)&(state==S1) has recall 1.0. Strongly gated by episode position: active through trials ~0-49 and essentially silent after trial ~55 (likely slow hidden-state drift), and by the previous trial being rewarded (94% of mass when prev_reward==1). The predicate D2 & S1 & ep_trial<50 & prev_reward==1 gets dev F1 0.84, mass recall 0.93. Magnitude is largest when S1 is reached by a rare transition after choosing a2 (a2->S1 is 19% of bottom-quartile activations but 58% of top-quartile ones; top windows are all a2->S1R, around 1.0, while common a1->S1 is around 0.1-0.4). Misses are mostly weak activations on S1 after an unrewarded trial. All variables are observed at D2.

issues: All factual claims reproduce. The unit fires 0 times at D1 or GO and only at D2 with state==S1: (phase==D2)&(state==S1) has recall 1.0 and precision 0.312. The ep_trial gate is real. Activation rate is 0.12 at trials 10-39, 0.069 at 40-49 and 0.014 at 50-59, with exactly 0 from trial 70 on. prev_reward==1 carries 93.7% of the mass. Test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.828, R 0.834, F1 0.831, mass recall 0.919).

Under the predicate, the a2->S1 (rare) case is almost pure (dev precision 0.983, recall 0.283, mass 0.40). The a1->S1 (common) case is weaker (precision 0.77, recall 0.56, mass 0.52). This fits the claim that rare arrivals at S1 give the largest activations.

There is a small systematic false-positive class. On a1->S1 trials right after switching from a2 (prev_action==2), precision is only 0.16, but this is just 1671 predicted steps. Excluding it lifts test F1 only from 0.831 to 0.841.

There is a small systematic miss class: rare a2->S1 arrivals after an unrewarded trial (active rate 0.37, only 4.9% of mass). Adding it raises test F1 only to 0.842 (mass recall 0.971), at a cost in precision.

The trial-50 cutoff is a soft decay, not a hard edge. Precision drops to 0.52 on a1 trials at ep_trial>=40, and cutoffs of 45 or 55 score about the same (dev F1 0.82 / 0.816). The 'slow drift in the hidden state' reason is a guess the activations cannot test. Otherwise the remaining errors look scattered, and the activations fade over long streaks of rewarded a1->S1 trials.
The predicate uses no future variables, and the label matches the predicate without overclaiming.
